subject: hedgehog
pitch: A plump hedgehog out on an autumn evening walk. A dome of spines in chestnut brown with cream tips, a soft fawn face with a pointed, twitchy snout, a shiny black button nose, tiny round ears and bright beady eyes. Little pink paws, and a single red maple leaf stuck on its spines like a trophy.
reasoning:
I'm planning the hedgehog's proportions and skeleton structure, setting up joints for the spine, head, jaw, and four legs with a compact rigging approach.

For the body I'll use a loft with tapered stations shaping a rounded chestnut-colored torso, then scatter spikes across the surface using small banded sweeps (brown base, cream tip) while watching the part budget to stay under roughly 1000 total pieces.

Settling on around 260 three-sided spikes for a reasonable count, filtering scatter points to avoid the face area and tilting each spike backward along the surface normal with a slight bias.

Bumping scatter count to 280 with tighter minDist. Planning a chestnut underlay beneath the spine dome with fawn countershading on the belly and underside. Now sketching the head as a tapering snout loft from base to nose, with a black nose sphere and small black eye spheres.

Adding ears, a separate lower jaw piece, and a head joint, then starting the leg structure with capsule shapes for limbs and flattened toe-studded paw spheres, chained to hip joints...

I'm checking that paw bottoms and body proportions align so feet sit flush at ground level, adjusting body height and center so the overall silhouette stays proportionate, though total height with spikes feels slightly tall for a hedgehog.

Now I'm designing a maple leaf shape to place on the back spikes, defining its five-lobed outline using a polar function with alternating radius values to create a non-self-intersecting star-like silhouette, then extruding it with thickness and placing it tilted at the upper back.

Still building lobe geometry and vein rods...

I'll place the leaf near the top of the body, slightly tilted, letting it poke through the spikes since that's close enough visually. For the eyes I'll add small sphere helpers with appropriate colors, skip whiskers and face markings for simplicity, and add a pink paw plus a tiny tail stub.

For the head, I'm using a swept loft bound to a "head" bone with rounded end caps, painting the snout with a fawn-to-cream gradient. I need to keep the body and head proportions distinct so the head stands out in front, and filter which spikes appear near the face based on z-position and normal direction so the brow area stays clear.

Now I'm defining the spike placement and jaw geometry: setting up scatter filters for spike density across the body surface, calling spike functions with tip points and bone bindings, then laying out the skeleton joints (root, body, head, jaw) with their positions and a small lower jaw capsule, adjusting the snout loft dimensions to match.

Adding ears and eye highlights, then setting up leg joints with capsule bones.
